solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Wader limb dips periodically (4)

indicatorNotes.periodically: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: the even letters of lImB dIpS

annotation.surface: A long-legged bird dunks one leg into the water every so often.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wader' in a crossword is nearly always a wading bird, not a person in boots.
annotation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird.

entries.clue: How to make techie start conversation? (5,3,3)

blocks.note: read as a recipe: the answer, taken as an instruction, rearranges some letters into the word TECHIE
the straight definition, an everyday idiom for getting strangers talking

annotation.surface: Advice on getting a shy computer geek to chat.
annotation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the answer is itself an instruction. BREAK tells you to jumble THE ICE, which makes TECHIE, the word in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: cracking the frozen surface stands for ending an awkward silence between strangers.

entries.clue: Spot crown jewels kings must leave for display (9)

indicatorNotes.must leave: the kings go out of the word, so remove both Ks

blocks.note: both are slang for a man's genitals
K = king; take the K out of SPECK and of TACKLE

annotation.surface: Someone spots the crown jewels being put on show once the kings have gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crown jewels' looks like the Tower of London regalia; here it is a cheeky euphemism, as is TACKLE. SPECKTACKLE loses both Ks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a striking show put on for an audience.

entries.clue: Read an involved letter that stimulates (10)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a relative clause standing for 'something that stimulates'

indicatorNotes.involved: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: a line is a short letter, as in 'drop me a line'

annotation.surface: Someone reads an intricate letter that gets the pulse racing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a single character of the alphabet; it is a note, a LINE. The definition leans on the clue's last two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone that stimulates the body into fight or flight.

entries.clue: Squeeze beneath a horse: it makes gelding niggled (7)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, RAM is placed below A NAG

blocks.note: the article kept as it is
a nag is an old horse
to ram is to squeeze or cram in

annotation.surface: Squashed under a horse, you'd be as irritated as a gelded one.
annotation.walkthrough: GELDING and NIGGLED use the same letters, so the definition is a worked example of the answer. The horse imagery makes 'gelding' look like part of the stable scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Rearranging GELDING gives NIGGLED, and such a rearrangement is an anagram.

entries.clue: Dancing dad sang with cast iron bucket (4,4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.Dancing: letters that dance move about, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Dad dances and sings, banging on a cast-iron bucket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' looks like a noun sitting with the cast iron; it is the verb, as in 'it's bucketing down'.
annotation.definitionFit: To bucket down and to rain cats and dogs both mean to pour with rain.

entries.clue: Glory in making return to sack Assad’s capital city (7)

indicatorNotes.making return: returning means going back, so the letters are reversed
indicatorNotes.to sack: to sack is to dismiss, so A is thrown out

blocks.note: glory = heaven, as in 'gone to glory'
Assad's capital letter is A; remove it from HEAVEN

annotation.surface: Revelling in the return of a sacked capital, Assad's.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital city' reads as one phrase; 'capital' belongs to Assad and means his first letter A, leaving just 'city' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ancient Assyrian capital on the Tigris, near modern Mosul in Iraq.

entries.clue: Still upset — not very (5)

indicatorNotes.not: not very means without V, so remove it

blocks.note: to invert is to turn over, to upset

annotation.surface: Someone is still upset, though not very much.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still upset' reads as a continuing mood; 'still' is the definition, an adjective meaning motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lying motionless, with no power to move.

entries.clue: Content of less articulate literary work (5)

indicatorNotes.Content of: the content of a word is what is inside it, its middle letters

annotation.surface: A literary piece whose contents are less well expressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' reads as an adjective describing the work; it is a verb, SAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short prose composition on a single subject.

entries.clue: Information with note helping peer group (10)

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
a ration is a helping or portion

annotation.surface: Information and notes being handed round to help a group of peers.
annotation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British English for information, as in 'get the gen'.
annotation.definitionFit: A generation is everyone of roughly the same age, your peer group.

entries.clue: Where man might eat dog’s breakfast? (4)

blocks.note: 'man' is a serviceman; think of the military dining hall
British slang for a muddle or shambles

annotation.surface: Wondering where a man might eat his dog's breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a serviceman; a military dining hall is a mess. 'Dog's breakfast' reads as pet food but is British slang for a muddle.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the forces' communal dining room, and a British idiom for a shambles.

entries.clue: Curry was one of fish and rice originally (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally points to where a word starts, its first letter

blocks.note: the skate is a flat fish

annotation.surface: A curry of fish and rice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Curry' looks like a dish, and fish and rice back that up; it is John Curry, the British figure skater who won Olympic gold in 1976.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: John Curry was an Olympic figure-skating champion.

entries.clue: City chap shot around noon (8)

indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the chap and the shot wrap themselves either side of N

blocks.note: cove is old British slang for a man
to have a shot is to have a try

annotation.surface: A man in the City is shot at midday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like London's financial district, where a City chap works; it is the definition. Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a cathedral city in the English Midlands.

entries.clue: Persuasive speaker can hire trio to play (11)

indicatorNotes.to play: letters at play are moved about

annotation.surface: A smooth talker is able to hire a trio to play a gig.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' pulls towards music with the trio; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one skilled in the art of persuasive speech.

entries.clue: Sweet cold wine lacking finish (4)

indicatorNotes.lacking finish: the word without its finish is missing its last letter

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
HOCK, a German white wine, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A sweet, chilled wine without much of an aftertaste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finish' sounds like wine-tasting talk for aftertaste; it means the last letter. Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
annotation.definitionFit: A choc is an informal word for a chocolate, a sweet.

entries.clue: Dating app perhaps pairing Lucifer with God? (10)

blocks.note: a lucifer is an old word for a match

annotation.surface: A dating app that sets the Devil up with God.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lucifer' looks like the Devil, facing God; it is an old name for a friction match.
annotation.definitionFit: A dating app is one example of a matchmaker, bringing couples together.

entries.clue: Scent stabiliser from Big Ears and Mr Messy (9)

indicatorNotes.Messy: a messy arrangement is jumbled, so rearrange

annotation.surface: Two children's characters, Big Ears from Noddy and Mr Messy from the Mr Men, make a perfume ingredient.
annotation.walkthrough: Big Ears is Noddy's friend in Enid Blyton's books and Mr Messy one of the Mr Men; 'Messy' splits off to be the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Ambergris, from sperm whales, is used to fix scents in perfume.

entries.clue: Officer vain at heart gave up backing a politician (4-2-4)

indicatorNotes.at heart: the heart of a word is its middle

annotation.surface: A vain officer gave up supporting a politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting the politician; it is the reversal instruction for CEDED.
annotation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer who assists a senior commander.

entries.clue: Close to safe area in dangerous Hebridean island (7)

indicatorNotes.Close to: the close of a word is its end, its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so the area letter sits within the word for dangerous

annotation.surface: Near safety, but in danger on a Scottish island.
annotation.walkthrough: Eriskay is a small island in the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small island of the Outer Hebrides, famous for Whisky Galore.

entries.clue: Persistently ask relatives for fruit (7)

blocks.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently

annotation.surface: Someone keeps asking their family for fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: Botanically a pumpkin is a fruit, which is why 'fruit' is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is botanically a fruit, a large gourd.

entries.clue: Drunk wanting to destroy (4)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so TO is taken away

blocks.note: blotto is British slang for very drunk

annotation.surface: A drunk itching to smash something up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting to' reads as desiring; 'wanting' is lacking, and 'to' is the very letters lost.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by way of 'blot out': to obliterate, wipe from existence.

entries.clue: Sons in slippery conditions turn Zephyr (4,4)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so the sons' letter goes within the slippery conditions

annotation.surface: Sons skidding on wet roads turn their Ford Zephyr.
annotation.walkthrough: The Zephyr was a Ford car, which suits the slippery road and the turning; here it is the west wind, named after the Greek god Zephyrus.
annotation.definitionFit: Classical naming: Zephyrus was the Greek god of the breeze from the west, and zephyr still names it.

entries.clue: Despicable person supporting women’s revolution (5)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, HEEL sits below W and holds it up

blocks.note: W = women, as on a lavatory door

annotation.surface: A cad backing a women's uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' plays at politics with the women's movement; it is a turn, a WHEEL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one full turn, as a wheeling bird or soldiers wheeling about.

entries.clue: Offence reduced financial support for part of Asia (5)

indicatorNotes.reduced: a reduced word is cut short, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: Cutting financial aid to part of Asia is an offence.
annotation.walkthrough: Sinai is the peninsula of Egypt that lies east of the Suez Canal, so in Asia though Egypt is African.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sinai peninsula is the part of Egypt that lies in Asia.

entries.clue: Gloomy note written about world and its end? (6)

indicatorNotes.written about: about means surrounding, so the note is written either side of the world
indicatorNotes.its end: the end of world is its last letter

blocks.note: mi is a note in sol-fa
an orb is a globe, the world

annotation.surface: A gloomy note about the world and its end.
annotation.walkthrough: The apocalyptic surface is itself gloomy, which hides the definition in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Morbid means gloomy, dwelling on death.

entries.clue: Master of fishing vessel we’re told? (4)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: what we are told we hear, so go by sound

blocks.note: an urn is a vessel, such as a tea urn; the bird's name is said the same way

annotation.surface: Hearsay about the skipper of a fishing boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fishing vessel' reads as a trawler with a master aboard; the split falls after 'fishing', and the master of fishing is the sea eagle.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the white-tailed sea eagle snatches fish from the water, so it is a master of fishing.

entries.clue: Boss reported Irish county club (10)

indicatorNotes.reported: reported means spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: a boss is a knob or stud

annotation.surface: The boss is said to belong to an Irish county club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society in Kerry; it is a weapon. A knobkerrie is a short knobbed stick from southern Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: A knobkerrie is a short wooden club with a knob at one end.

entries.clue: Saw that could be done easily (4,4,2)

indicatorNotes.could be: the letters could be something else when rearranged

annotation.surface: A saw that makes the job easy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a proverb; it is the past tense of see.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for the past tense of see: to have caught sight of something.

entries.clue: Degenerate bore (4)

blocks.note: a verb here: to decline, go downhill morally
a verb here: to drill a well or mineshaft

annotation.surface: A degenerate bore.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns for dull, sleazy people; both are verbs here.
annotation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: to fall to a lower moral state, and to drive a shaft down into the ground.
